problem:
Find the radius of convergence $R$ for the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{(x-3)^{n}}{(2n)!}=1+\frac{(x-3)}{2!}+\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{4!}+\frac{(x-3)^{3}}{6!}+⋯\,.
$$
worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test. we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{(x-3)^{n}}{(2n)!}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(x-3)^{n+1}}{[2(n+1)]!}\cdot \frac{(2n)!}{(x-3)^{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(x-3)}{(2n+2)(2n+1)}| \\  & =|x-3|{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{1}{(2n+2)(2n+1)} \\  & =|x-3|\cdot 0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied for all $-\infty <x<\infty .$ Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=\infty .$
